title: CJP holds Tiranga march and counter-protest in Delhi
seoTitle: Delhi CJP Tiranga march and protest

tea.why: Protesters marched to show solidarity with detained leaders and voice opposition to the Chief Election Commissioner.
tea.want: Demanded the resignation of the CEC, rollback of the electoral roll revision, and repeal of the 2023 Election Commissioner Appointment Act.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Police detained about 150 protesters in central Delhi following flash protests and a counter-demonstration.

summary: On October 16, 2026, supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organizations held flash protests and a Tiranga march in central Delhi, specifically around Connaught Place and Mandi House, after police denied permission for the planned event. The demonstrators carried the Tricolour and the Preamble of the Constitution while raising anti-Chief Election Commissioner slogans. A counter-demonstration was staged by local shopkeepers near Palika Bazar who chanted pro-government slogans and stated that the protests were disrupting their businesses. Minor altercations occurred as police attempted to disperse the crowds. Authorities detained approximately 150 people, including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and All-India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora. The opposition criticized the detentions, while the Central Government characterized the protests as an attempt to cause anarchy and regime change.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Rollback of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
Withdrawal of the 2023 Election Commissioner Appointment Act
response: The police denied permission for the march, deployed security personnel, and preventively detained around 150 protesters, including key leaders. The BJP-led Central Government termed the protest an attempt to bring about regime change by using young people to spread anarchy.

arrests.text: police detained around 150 people during a series of flash protests

updates.text: CJP supporters carried out a Tiranga march and flash protests in Delhi following denied permission.
Police detained around 150 participants, including prominent student and party leaders, amidst minor altercations.
